newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian markets shrug off cabinet changes, for now.
newsitem.headline: Russian markets shrug off cabinet changes, for now.

text.p: Russia's cabinet re-shuffle got a cool reception on local markets on Monday, with personnel changes largely factored into prices, dealers said.
But they did not rule out the possibility of a more positive reaction soon, as investors mulled top personnel changes and their implications for the economy more closely.

"All the recent good news has been priced in since Chubais was appointed First Deputy Prime Minister, although today's names are very attractive for the clients," said Pavel Gronbjerg, head corporate securities trader at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Moscow.
President Boris Yeltsin on Monday named Boris Nemtsov, a liberal reformist governor of Nizhny Novgorod region, First Deputy Prime Minister.
Interfax news agency quoted Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin as saying that First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais would also be Finance Minister.
Chubais was shifted to the government from the post of head of the Kremlin administration on March 7.
Chernomyrdin reaffirmed Alfred Kokh's position as privatisation minister and awarded him with a Deputy Prime Minister post.
Chernomyrdin also promoted Yakov Urinson to Economy Minister and Deputy Prime Minister from First Deputy Economy Minister.
The last two appointments came after the markets had closed, but markets largely shrugged off the appointments of Nemtsov and Chubais, as they had been anticipated.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares edged by 0.3 percent to 330.38 on total market volume of $30.62 million.
Energy utility UES closed at $0.2255 after $0.2256 at Friday's close, while Gazprom, the natural gas monopoly, closed unchanged at $0.655.
Regional power utility Lenenergo turned in the best performance of the day, rising to $0.945 from $0.870.
However, traders said they expected prices to trend higher over the summer, and were increasing positions gradually.
Russian dollar-denominated MinFin bonds edged down, reflecting a general downward trend in emerging markets paper.

"Prices eased earlier on foreign selling as the general (emerging market) trend is down. The day was otherwise quiet," an International Moscow Bank dealer said, adding that the new-look government could help revive the market.
On the government securities market, prices edged down in thin volume as buyers waited for lower values.
"Operators were not in a hurry to invest as there was much money on the market on Friday, but prices did not rise," said United City Bank chief trader Mikhail Grigoryev.
The average yield edged up to 31.1 percent from 30.0 percent on Friday.
The rouble, tightly controlled by the Central Bank, firmed on Monday as banks anticipated a rouble shortage ahead of Wednesday's Treasury bill sales.
The rouble was traded at 5,703-05 to the U.S. dollar, with overnight credits falling to 5-10 percent from 20-30 percent on Friday.
